column5: A parishioner's statue bought in Thailand wept rose oil from 2002 and was put on display in the church. University scientists could not explain it.

column3: Our Lady of the Turning Eyes
column5: During a French siege in the Thirty Years' War, more than 40 witnesses said the statue turned pale, raised its eyes and later shed tears. It was moved to the Münster in 1802.
A painting brought from Ireland by an exiled bishop is said to have wept blood for three hours on St Patrick's Day 1697, watched by a large crowd.

A village icon wept for weeks in 1696 and was taken by the Emperor to St Stephen's Cathedral, Vienna, where it still hangs. The copy left behind at Máriapócs is said to have wept in 1715 and 1905. Hungary's main pilgrimage site.
A statue wept for over three months from 2017.
People gathered to pray around a statue that appeared to weep red liquid in 2020.

column3: Madonna delle Lacrime (Our Lady of Tears)
column5: A mass-produced plaster plaque of Mary above a couple's bed wept for four days in August-September 1953. Church chemists said the liquid matched human tears. The plaque is now in a huge modern sanctuary built for it.

A wooden statue at a small convent wept 101 times between 1975 and 1981, and a TV crew filmed it in 1978. It is linked to messages reported by Sister Agnes Sasagawa and is the best-known approved weeping statue.
A statue at a hilltop prayer site near a Bronze Age ruin has been reported weeping blood, oil and salt since 2006. The church has not recognised it.

column3: Our Lady Mediatrix of All Grace, Tanauan
column5: A statue was found with blood on its face and oil in its palm.
Villagers reported blood-like traces near the image's eyes and said its hands had unclasped.
A statue owned by Julia Kim began weeping in June 1985 and later wept blood. The local church rejects it and Asian bishops still warn pilgrims away, but the shrine stays busy.

column3: Sweating St John of La Laguna
column5: A painting of St John was said to sweat during a plague epidemic in 1648.

column3: Weeping statue of Catholic Martyrs Church
column5: An outdoor statue at a Vietnamese parish seemed to weep red liquid in November 2005; it came back each time it was wiped away.

column3: Weeping icon of St Nicholas, Chicago
column5: An icon began to weep in December 1986 and 19 other icons in the church later followed. It stopped in 1987 and started again a year later.
The icon wept during Lent in April 1994. Over a million visitors came in 20 years, and the street outside was later renamed after the icon.
A bronze statue began weeping in 2018. Diocesan tests found rose-scented olive oil but no hidden source.
Statues were said to weep in the presence of a young associate pastor, Fr James Bruse, who also reported stigmata. Thousands visited in 1992.
